rounds.text: Sky Gold & Diamonds Ltd carries significant valuation and cash generation risks that are not supported by the underlying cash flows. The company trades at an expensive P/E of 46.4 [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 8.86x [E2], with a discounted cash flow model estimating intrinsic value at Rs 560 against a market price of Rs 638, leaving a negative margin of safety of -13.9% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, despite reporting profits, cash generation has broken down completely: operating cash flow for March 2026 is negative at Rs -24 Cr [E33], free cash flow stands at Rs -64 Cr [E34], and cash conversion reads an alarming -0.11x [E32]. This disconnect is compounded by rising borrowings, which increased to Rs 644 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 517 Cr a year earlier [E37], and a heavy promoter sell-off that saw insider holdings drop by 21.81 percentage points down to 51.74% [E39]. Conceded: [E14, E15, E16, E17, E18, E19, E20, E21, E22, E23, E48, E49, E50, E63, E64, E65, E66, E67].
